en.headline: Department of Justice launches HK$20,000 lawtech subscription scheme
en.dek: Small law firms and newly qualified barristers can claim up to HK$20,000 for one-year subscriptions to designated legal technology services until 29 January.
body: The Department of Justice has launched a funding scheme offering up to HK$20,000 to help small and medium-sized law firms and newly qualified barristers subscribe to legal technology tools.

Deputy Secretary for Justice Horace Cheung said on Thursday the pilot scheme would lower the barrier for practitioners to adopt technology in legal research, document drafting, workflow management and hearing support. Applications are open until 29 January 2027 and are managed by the Law Society of Hong Kong and the Hong Kong Bar Association.

Eligible applicants include sole practitioners, Hong Kong law firms with five or fewer partners, and barristers with no more than seven years of call. They may choose from a list of 14 local, mainland and overseas providers. Reimbursement is on an actual-expense basis after subscription.

Cheung said he hoped the financial incentive would encourage wider use of the tools and that the department would monitor the pilot and consider further measures. The Bar Association said the scheme could benefit about 500 members.

zh.headline: 律政司推出兩萬元法律科技訂購資助計劃
zh.dek: 中小型律師事務所及年資較淺大律師可獲最多兩萬元資助，訂購一年指定法律科技服務，申請期至明年1月29日。
body: 律政司推出資助計劃，向中小型律師事務所及年資較淺的大律師提供最多兩萬元，資助訂購法律科技工具。
律政司副司長張國鈞周四表示，試點計劃旨在降低業界採用科技的門檻，涵蓋法律研究、文件草擬、工作流程管理及聽訊支援。申請期至2027年1月29日，由香港律師會及香港大律師公會管理。
合資格申請人包括獨資執業、不多於五名合夥人的香港律師事務所，以及執業年資不超過七年的大律師。申請人可從14家本地、內地及海外供應商名單中選擇服務，按實報實銷方式在訂購後獲發還款項。
張國鈞說，希望以財務誘因鼓勵更多人使用有關工具，律政司會監察試點進展並考慮進一步措施。大律師公會表示計劃可惠及約500名會員。
